work.text: Although Daumier was particularly inspired by the troubadour paintings of French Rococo artist Jean-Antoine Watteau of the 1700s, he rendered the subject here in a powerful style of simplified, muscular form that appealed to modern artists of his own time.
Perceptive sympathy of a similar, though of a less ecstatic, kind distinguishes Daumier’s pictures of strolling players.

source.author: Michael Sadleir
source.title: Daumier: The Man and the Artist

moment.text: The troubadour, a medieval traveling poet and entertainer, was a popular subject in 19th-century French art. Associated with chivalry and courtly love, the theme reflects a broader, romantic fascination with France's medieval past.
On the base, where the contemplative symbols generally find a place, I would put four artists : Millet, Cezanne, Meunier, and Van Gogh ; all in the reverent attitude of worship.
